explanation: Its style is Elizabethan, built on an Italian chord pattern that reached England after Henry died in 1547. The song was registered for printing in London in 1580.

claims.text: There is no evidence that Henry VIII wrote Greensleeves.
Greensleeves is in an Elizabethan style, based on an Italian chord pattern.
The Italian style that Greensleeves uses reached England after Henry VIII's death in 1547.
Greensleeves was registered for publication in London in 1580.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: Main argument: The Wikipedia article calls the Henry VIII attribution a common myth, because the tune rests on an Italian compositional style that only reached England after his death in 1547 (It is a common myth that Greensleeves was written by King Henry VIII. However, Henry could not have written Greensleeves, as the piece is based on an Italian style of composition that did not reach England until after his death.). The Henry VIII article is similarly firm, saying it is certain he did not.

claimResults.note: Quoted from the named Wikipedia article 'Greensleeves' (Tier B), and no source found contradicts it. The summary adds that the detailed dating is thinly sourced ('Only the Henry VIII attribution is firmly rejected'), and search 8 (Britannica, British Library, Library of Congress) was silent on the timing. So c3 rests on one Tier B source: enough for a high-risk practice claim under section 9.5.2, and no more.

issues.note: c3 rests on a single Tier B source (Wikipedia). The Tier A library pages and Britannica found say nothing either way about when the Italian ground reached England. Acceptable for a practice item, and a good candidate for the seeded audit.
